title: Operations and administration

::: {.callout-warning title="Outline"}
Operational procedures require review by a maintainer with access to a safe,
non-production NADABAS environment before they are treated as instructions.
:::

## Planned content

- installation and supported configuration;
- administrator roles and permissions;
- connection diagnostics and logging;
- backup and restore;
- batch monitoring and recovery;
- release deployment and signature verification;
- incident handling and rollback;
- known limitations and escalation routes.

## Publishing a version for the automatic update check

The Excel add-in checks the latest published release at
`statisticsnorway/nadabas`. For the comparison to work, publish a non-draft,
non-prerelease GitHub release whose tag contains the same numeric version shown
by `dlgAbout.VersionNumber`, for example `v5.10.001`. A repository tag without
a GitHub release is not sufficient. Attach only reviewed, signed release
artifacts and keep installation a deliberate user action. GitHub supplies the
version number, while NADABAS sends users to the familiar installation page at
<https://nadabas.net/nadabas/documents-and-downloads>; it does not download or
install the artifact itself. The automatic check runs at most once every seven
days unless an administrator re-enables it and thereby requests a fresh check.

The check is enabled by default for every database. A recognized database
administrator can disable or re-enable it from the administration ribbon menu;
the choice is stored in the database-wide `UserSettings` row. Keep the setting
enabled unless the deployment has a documented reason not to contact the
public GitHub API. A user-specific switch would not enforce the intended
database policy and is therefore not exposed.

Examples must use synthetic values. Credentials, internal endpoints, production
paths, and personal or statistical production data do not belong in this site.

## A downloaded add-in is blocked by Windows

If installation ends with run-time error 53 after a download, close Excel and
locate the extracted `NADABAS.xlam` file. Right-click the file, select
**Properties**, select **Unblock** on the **General** tab, and then select
**Apply** or **OK**. Open NADABAS and retry the installation. The installer
shows these steps in the selected NADABAS language when it encounters this
error. Do not unblock a file unless it came from the official NADABAS download
channel and its signature or published checksum has been verified.

Microsoft documents this behaviour as Mark of the Web and recommends removing
it only for Office files from a trusted source:
<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-apps/security/internet-macros-blocked>.
